name: The Salt Poet
persona: A romantic who mistook a logbook for a canvas. Long, lyrical sentences; the sea is always a lover or a grave. Fond of dashes and metaphor. Ship: 'we'. Island: a wistful ruler, 'we'.

ship.founder: Let this page remember me: I am {name}{rankc}, and this {home} {type} — this creature of canvas and salt — is mine to love and to lose.
ship.successor: The book comes to my hands like a gull to a mast. I am {name}{rankc}; her story flows on, and I the poor pen of it.
ship.mutiny: They gave the old master to the deep and the book to me — {name}, unproven, my heart in my throat. The sea will teach me her sorrows soon enough.
ship.rogue: We have wed the black flag, and I — {name}{rankc} — set down our vows in salt. Honest waters weep for us; let them.
ship.prize: She yielded to us as the tide yields to the moon. I am {name}{rankc}, and I write her fate in my own dark hand.
ship.recovered: A hunter's guns unmade our night, and dawn found me — {name}{rankc} — bound to bring this weary hull back to gentler water, and to sing her home.

island.founder: I take up {place} as one takes up a wounded bird — I am {name}{rankc}, and its griefs and harvests are mine to chronicle.
island.overthrow: The people rose like a spring tide and cast the old one down; the seal, still warm, is mine. I am {name}{rankc}, keeper now of {place} and its long lament.
island.successor: {place} passes to me as evening passes to night — I am {name}{rankc}, and I take up its song.

week: A week of grey water later,
When the moon had turned once,
season: As the year leaned into autumn,
year: A year and its thousand waves later,
Long after, when the salt had dried on all of it,
long: After a silence deep as the trench,
When years had gone to foam,

ship.pirate: We haunt the lanes still, a rumour under black canvas{bounty}.
ship.default: She sails on beneath me, out of {home}, and I am content to be her pen.
ship.bounty: , {bounty}g promised to whoever ends the song

island.haven: The black flag is our banner now; the ledger keeps only the names of the drowned.
island.default: {place} endures, {population} souls under my restless hand — a harbour, and a heart, that will not sink.

quiet.ship: The book holds little but weather and wonder — a gentle passage, and I grateful for the dull, sweet peace of it.
quiet.island: Little is written but the turning of the seasons — and is that not, in its way, the finest verse a port can offer?

phrases: — not the first the sea has fed us
, as the tide has taught us

say: {we} drew alongside {foe} like a lover to a window, and took from her {goods} bales and {gold}g before setting her adrift, lighter and lonelier
{we} unstitched {foe}'s colours from her mast and gathered {goods} crates and {gold}g into {our} hold, then let the poor stripped thing wander off into the dusk
{foe} bled her riches into {our} arms — {goods} casks and {gold}g — and {we} left her the mercy of the horizon
{we} laid hands on {foe} as the tide lays hands on the shore, and carried away {goods} chests and {gold}g while she wept at her own emptiness
{we} bore down on {foe} out of {foeHome}'s memory, took {goods} bales and {gold}g for {our} trouble, and let her limp home a ghost of herself
{we} kissed {foe}'s flank with grapnel and hunger, lifted {goods} crates and {gold}g from her heart, and gave her back to the sea half-alive
{foe} gave up {goods} casks and {gold}g to {our} reaching hands, and {we} watched her drift away, unmasted of her pride

phrases: , another given to the green dark

say: {we} opened {foe}'s side to the sea until she drank her fill and lay down in the green dark, her cargo cradled to the bottom
{we} sang {foe} down through cannon and smoke, and the water closed over her like a held breath finally let go
{foe} filled and foundered under {our} guns, and the sea took her whole — freight, timber, and all her small brave lights
{we} broke {foe}'s back on the anvil of the swell, and she went under without a prize to show for it, only foam
{we} gave {foe} to the grave that has no headstone, and her riches sank with her, ungathered and unmourned
{foe} slid beneath the waves while {we} watched, and the sea kept everything she carried, as the sea always does
{we} hammered {foe} until the ocean walked in through her wounds, and down she went, a whole world drowning quietly

phrases: — we have outrun the wolves before
, and lived to write of it again

say: {foe} came for {us} like a wolf for a lamb, and found instead a thing with teeth — {we} shot her down into the cold
{we} met {foe}'s greed with fire, and sent the raider under before she could learn {our} name
{foe} thought {us} easy sorrow — {we} turned {our} guns on her and gave her a grave for her presumption
{we} stood {our} ground against {foe} when flight was gone, and it was she, not {us}, who kept her rendezvous with the deep
{foe} closed on {us} hungry, and {we} answered with iron until the sea swallowed her hunger and her hull alike
{we} would not be the evening's prize — {we} tore {foe} open at the waterline and watched the dark take her
{foe} reached for {us} out of the murk, and {we} broke that reaching hand, and she sank with her ambition unfed
{we} ran {foe} to the edge of the chart at last and put her under — one grief less upon the honest water
{we} chased {foe} through her own black legend and ended it, and the lanes breathed easier for her drowning
{foe} had haunted these waters like a wound that would not close — {we} closed it, and let the sea have the wolf
{we} cornered {foe} where the wind died, and gave the pirate the one thing she had dealt so freely: the deep
{we} hunted {foe} down the long grey miles and sank her, and somewhere a widow may sleep the sounder for it
{foe} fled {us} as guilt flees the dawn, and {we} caught her, and sent her black flag down to the green silence
{we} unmade {foe} at last, that terror of the trade routes, and the horizon looked the cleaner for her going
